:JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 01.02.2023 at about 5.30 p.m., the Petitioner was proceeding towards his residence at Bakshi Garden on Dr.T.C.M.Rayan Road, (Goodshed road) while crossing the said road near Ayyappa Swamy temple, at that time, the rider of two wheeler/Honda Activa bearing No.KA-02-HP-2853 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Srinivasa hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was studying in 4th standard.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. Despite of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed objection to the main petition.
4. Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle.

Further it contended that the accident was caused solely due to negligence of the petitioner who was crossing the road where there is no zebra crossing and not due to the negligence on the part of driver of the motor cycle.
Further contended that owner of the insured motor cycle has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it contended that the rider of the vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license to ride the vehicle and the owner of the motor cycle entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid driving licence.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
Anish.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 01.02.2023 at about 5.30 p.m., on Dr.T.C.M Royan road near Ayyappa swamy temple, Cottonpet, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of rider of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-02-HP-2853?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.17.
He also got examined doctor as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P-18 to 22 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondents have not adduced any evidence.

7. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 8. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 01.02.2023 at about 5.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02- HP-2853 by its rider.
9.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-HP-2853 by its rider.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, natural guardian of the petitioner/father is examined as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-17.
P.W.1 has re- iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.
Ex. P-1
to Ex.P-6
are the true copies of FIR, complaint, spot panchanama along with sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
Ex . P.7
and 8 are notarised copy of aadhar cards.
Ex . P.9
is study certificate, Ex.P.10 is discharge summaries.

Ex.P.11 is Lab report, Ex.P.12 is medical bills, Ex.P.13 is advance receipts and medical bill payment receipts,
Ex.P.14 is prescriptions, Ex.P.15 is photographs, Ex.P.16 is CD and Ex.P.17 is X-rays.
Anish.

3 11.

Upon going through Ex.P-1 and 2 FIR and Complaint, same is evident that on the complaint lodged before Chickpet Traffic Police station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-HP-2853 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

Ex.P.3 is the copy of Spot panchanama along with sketch justifies that same is drawn in the presence of panchas, it further justifies that while petitioner was crossing the road the offending vehicle hit him and caused accident.

Ex.P.4 is the copy of IMV report justify the fact of involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and the said document also discloses that the cause of accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in question.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of wound certificate discloses that as a result of RTA the petitioner sustained grievous.

Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet discloses the fact that after thorough investigation IO has charge sheeted the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-HP- 2853 for the offences punishable under Secs.279, 338 of IPC.
12.
PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.
During his cross examination he has denied that there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending Scooter.
13. Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the rider of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02- HP-2853 and in the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
14. Issue No

. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-HP-2853 by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15. In the petition, the PW.1 has shown the age of the petitioner as 11 years.
He has produced Aadhar card and study certificate at Ex.P.8 and 9 to prove his age.
As per the these document, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 26.01.2013.
The accident has taken place on 01.02.2023.

Hence,
the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was taken as 10 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
16.
According to the Petitioner, he had sustained comminuted fracture of left tibia and fibula.
In this regard, next friend of the Petitioner, his father deposed as PW-2 and relied on the Wound Certificate at Ex.P5.

As per the Wound Certificate, the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling RM Tenderness pain over left lower limb.
X-ray shows left leg both bone fracture
The doctor has opined that injury is grievous in nature.
The PW.1 deposed that his son was admitted as an inpatient from 01.02.2023 to 15.02.2023.

4
Further, petitioner got examined Dr.Avinash Parthaswarathy as PW.2.
He has also reiterated the same in his evidence and got marked Ex.P.18 to 22 i.e., OP slip, disability assessment proforma, case sheet and X-ray.
In the cross examination he has admitted that fractures are united and the condition of the petitioner was improved.
Implants are still in-- situ and are not affecting to the movements and the bone development is normal as petitioner is in tender age.
He has denied the other suggestions.
He has admitted that he has assessed physical disability only.
The age of the Petitioner is 11 years.
As such question of occupation and income does not arise.
In the circumstances, any disability shown to his limb cannot be assessed as functional disability.
17. According to the evidence of doctor/PW-2, the minor Petitioner suffered physical impairment in left lower limb is 41% and to the whole body disability is 14%.

In a decision passed in Civil Appeal No.7139/2013 (Master Mallikarjun Vs Division Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., and another)
by the Hon'ble Apex Court, it is held that if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, the minor Petitioner would be entitled for compensation of Rs.3 lakhs in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendance etc., towards conventional heads like pain and sufferings already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship inconvenience,
discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs Division Manager, National Insurance Co., Ltd., and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As noted above,
there is assessment of whole body disability of the petitioner at 14%.

As such, having considered the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and its gravity it appears just and proper to this court to consider that the petitioner sustained whole body disability at the rate of 14%.
18.
The medical records and the evidence produced in support of the same disclose the fact that petitioner sustained fracture of left tibia and fibula.
Hence, there are certainly pain and sufferings.

As such, it appears just and proper to this court to award compensation of sum of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
(If it is between 10%-30%)

19. In addition to the compensation towards conventional heads, the minor Petitioner is also entitled for compensation under the heads like discomfort and inconvenience to the parents and their loss of earnings during the period of hospitalization of the Petitioner and towards medical expenditure.
With regard to the case on hand, the medical records disclose that discharge summary is produced.
The Ex.P.10 discharge summary, discloses the fact that petitioner was admitted at Srinivasa hospital from 01.02.2023 to 15.02.2023 and took treatment as an inpatient.
Upon consideration of the age of the petitioner, it is needless to mention that he might have been accompanied by his parents to the hospital during treatment.
As such, his parents might have lost their earnings during that period.
In the absence of proof of income of his parents, it would be lawful to award Rs.10,000/- as compensation towards loss of earnings and their discomfort.
20. With regard to medical expenditure, the PW.1 has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.2,60,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 65 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.12 which is totally amounting to Rs.2,42,719/-.
I have gone through the medical bills and the same are acceptable.
Hence, by rounding of the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,42,800/- as a compensation under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
Anish.S vs Sagar.

5 21.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering, Rs. 3,00,000/-
loss of amenities 2. Loss of income during Rs. 10,000/-
the laid up period Rs.2,42,800/-
3.
Medical expenditure Total Rs.5,52,800/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,52,800/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

22. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-HP-2853.

There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,52,800/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, entire award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank until he attains age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/father of the minor petitioner is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor petitioner.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
